subject: Follow-up: Procurement and Marketplace options
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Healy <tom@lumenai.com>, Sara Patel <sara.patel@lumenai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Procurement and Marketplace options

Hi Tom / Sara  great to meet earlier today. Thanks for walking through the use case and expected traffic patterns. Quick recap and the options we discussed so procurement can decide the path: 

1) Commercial paths (pricing & payment):
- Card (self-serve / immediate): good for POC and pilot (pay-as-you-go).
- PO / invoiced (procurement): supports net-30 / net-45, requires standard procurement paperwork and a purchase order.
- AWS Marketplace (preferred by many customers): can buy via SaaS contract or via marketplace procurement flow  often simplifies procurement approvals but may change invoicing cadence.

2) Procurement readiness (paper process):
- If you need vendor paperwork (W-9, DPA, SOC2 report), we can provide those today; legal can review and sign standard terms.
- For PO-based purchases we typically request a PO referencing the quote; we can accept PO to Redwood Dedicated or Hosted.

3) Marketplace details we discussed:
- We have an active AWS Marketplace listing (SaaS). GCP marketplace available on request; Azure is on the roadmap but not live today.
- Marketplace purchases often remove the need for Redwood-issued invoices depending on internal policies  procurement teams like the single-pane billing on AWS.

Attachments: I attached our pricing overview for AWS marketplace and a procurement checklist to accelerate internal approvals.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm whether procurement prefers PO or marketplace purchase?
- If PO, please share procurement contact and any standard vendor forms (I included a checklist that may help).
- If marketplace, confirm which cloud account/org you plan to use (AWS account ID or marketplace buyer/org).
- Ill loop in Marissa (CS lead) for SOW and onboarding timeline once purchase path is decided.

Happy to hop on a 20-min call with procurement if that speeds things up.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
camila_reyes@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-AWS-marketplace.pdf]
[Attachment: redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx]

From: Tom Healy <tom@lumenai.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Patel <sara.patel@lumenai.com>, procurement@lumenai.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:23:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Procurement and Marketplace options

Thanks, Camila  helpful recap. A few clarifying questions from procurement: 

1) Our default is PO for any vendor spend > $50k ARR; smaller pilots typically go on card. Is there anything special about purchasing via AWS Marketplace that procurement should know? Will Redwood invoice us directly if we buy through the AWS Marketplace or will it be billed through AWS (i.e., consolidated AWS bill)?

2) We prefer to get a single SOW + quote we can attach to the PO. Can your team produce a short SOW and include the quote line items (by model/ingress tokens/throughput) so procurement has a clear cost basis?

3) Timeline: procurement needs vendor validation (W-9), SOC2 report, and a completed vendor form (attached separately).

If AWS Marketplace means procurement can avoid a manual PO, that would be ideal, but some of our internal finance teams still require a direct vendor on file. Im looping procurement@lumenai.com on this thread  theyll provide the vendor form and preferred PO terms.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Tom

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Procurement and Marketplace options

Hi Tom / procurement team  thanks for the quick reply and the vendor form (Sara / procurement). Answers inline below and next steps: 

1) Marketplace billing mechanics:
- AWS Marketplace SaaS: you purchase via AWS and it shows up on your AWS bill; AWS pays Redwood on your behalf (so you wont get a separate Redwood invoice). This typically satisfies many companies that want consolidated billing via AWS.
- If you need Redwood to be the invoiced vendor (for PO reasons), we can do a direct PO with net-30 terms. Well accept PO referencing our quote and issue an invoice to LumenAI.

2) SOW / quote:
- Marissa (cc) can draft a short SOW + quote with the usage assumptions you provided (expected qps/throughput, token volume). Marissa  can you prepare a 1-page SOW + two purchase options (Marketplace SaaS and Direct PO) by Monday 6/15?

3) Compliance docs:
- Attached: W-9, SOC2 attestation summary, and the procurement checklist. If procurement needs the full SOC2 report well provide the signed report under NDA.

4) Marketplace availability:
- AWS marketplace: live (link below). If you want to transact via AWS well need the buyer AWS Account ID or Marketplace Org ID to prepare the listing quote.
- GCP Marketplace: available but requires a manual enablement step on our end  can be done in 12 weeks if you prefer GCP billing.
- Azure: not live today; we can flag as a future option but it will not help with immediate procurement.

Attachments referenced here: [Attachment: redwood-pricing-AWS-marketplace.pdf], [Attachment: redwood-procurement-checklist.xlsx], [Attachment: redwood-w9.pdf]

Next steps / action owners:
- Procurement (LumenAI): confirm preferred commercial path ("PO via Redwood" or "AWS Marketplace") and, if marketplace, provide AWS Account ID / Marketplace org.
- Marissa (Redwood): draft SOW + quote for both purchase paths by 6/15.
- Camila: schedule a 20-min call with procurement if they prefer to walk legal/finance through the marketplace flow.

Tom  if you want, I can get you a draft SOW now and Marissa can finalize after.

Thanks,
Camila
